title: Groundhog Day
scope: The 1993 film · representative stages of Phil’s repeating day
premise: Phil keeps waking up on the same morning. If the town forgets each day, what can change?
ending: The next morning finally arrives. The town has been repeating, but Phil has accumulated experience and changed the way he treats people. The film does not give an exact count of all his repeated days.

people.name: Phil Connors
people.introduction: A weather presenter who remembers days that everyone else forgets.

events.title: An ordinary assignment becomes a trap
events.text: Weather presenter Phil reports on Groundhog Day in Punxsutawney with his producer, Rita. A blizzard prevents the crew from leaving town.

events.title: The morning starts again
events.text: Phil wakes to the same alarm and finds the day repeating. Other people behave as though yesterday’s encounters have not happened. Phil remembers them.

events.title: He tests what the repetition lets him do
events.text: With no lasting consequences for the town, Phil pursues pleasure and uses remembered details to manipulate encounters. These attempts do not free him.

events.title: Knowing the day does not give him control
events.text: Phil’s attempts to escape the repetition fail. Even extreme actions lead back to the familiar morning.

events.title: Experience becomes a way to help
events.text: Phil develops skills and learns to respond to the people around him. Their day resets, but his practice and attention accumulate.

events.title: He spends the day caring for other people
events.text: Phil’s actions express the person he has become. His relationship with Rita is no longer just a sequence of tricks designed to obtain a particular response.
events.whenLabel: February 2 · the last repeated day shown

events.title: A different morning arrives
events.text: Phil wakes with Rita and discovers that time is moving forward again. The repeating day has ended.

chapters.title: Change within it
chapters.introduction: These are selected phases across many repetitions. Each card can cover several days; the guide does not assign a count to them.

sources.title: Danny Rubin on the length of the loop
sources.note: In this 20 December 2017 interview, Rubin declines to assign a number and discusses the removal of duration references. It supports leaving the day count unspecified; the interview does not verify the individual scenes below.

connections.label: The town returns to the same morning.
connections.retainedText: Phil remembers previous days. This example stands for the repetition that continues throughout the guide.

flowchart.title: Timeline flow chart
flowchart.description: Follow the changes Phil experiences while the town repeats the same day. The cards condense many repetitions. They do not create a new timeline for each day.
flowchart.frame: Selected phases across repeated days, followed by the new morning. This is not calendar order or a count of repetitions.
